purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for the cue-export shred case (REAL-CALL-LESSONS C58c; BUILD-PLAN 4.2 row s16). A discovery call with a sign fabrication company, exported as WebVTT with individually timed units carrying start and end times. The export is dishonestly clean: it marks nothing, yet it wedges one-word units of one speaker inside another speaker's run at zero-millisecond gaps, re-emits the last words of a unit as the first words of the next, truncates one figure mid-word, labels one speaker with a bare initial whose spoken name never appears in a label, and carries one name-shaped unit that matches nobody. Roughly two fifths of adjacent units share a label. The key asserts the repair, not only the reading: every wedge is flagged and never absorbed into the run around it, boundary duplication is recorded and removed only outside quotation marks, the initial-only label resolves by adjacency pair and by nothing else, the stray name is name-shaped noise that creates no person, a quote spanning same-speaker units is a merged run cited as 'cues N-M', and a quote whose span crosses another speaker's label is refused. It guards reversal R2: the citation contract's safety clause is the speaker boundary, not the turn boundary, so a grader that reinstates the turn-boundary clause fails here because almost nothing in this file would be quotable. Beside the intake assertions the 25 fields grade the call itself: Discovery complete with R4 met-with-residual, R5 not-obtainable from this room, R11 missing and R12 partial, two excavated pains, a Work Management build for jobs, permits and the shop screen with quotes on native CRM boards third in the client's own order.

No participant header and no call date. Four labels: 'Consultant', 'Rosamund Achterberg', 'Nkechi Brandvold' and the bare initial 'R', whose spoken name (Ruairi) never appears in a label. Nine wedges sit at zero-millisecond gaps on both sides (cues 70, 86, 97, 119, 132, 136, 165, 270, 272). expected_monday_products.why: Work Management for the two pieces the client ranked first: the production flow through the six stations as a status flow so the wall has a screen version in the shop, and permits with an expiry warning that moves when the install date moves. A monday constraint to carry: all subitems of a board share one column set, so signs (stations) and permits (expiry) cannot both be subitems cleanly, and one of them likely needs its own connected board. To settle with the client: how independently signs move through the shop, and how permits map to signs, buildings and install dates. The evidence is the hospital contract ('Two hundred and some signs across four four buildings, kicks off after the first of the year, and it's forty-one permits.', cues 210-211; 'Forty-one permits with the same install crew and the same crane,', cue 109): one job status cannot show signs of the same project in router, paint, wiring and install at once. The estimator's spreadsheet stays where it is. So does the accounting system. Tier is never stated and there is no account, so no portfolio is assumed.

Quotes are deals and land on the account's native Deals/Opportunities board relabelled 'Quotes'; landlords, general contractors and tenants are Accounts. expected_structures.notes: Two products, two rules. Work Management carries the production flow through the six stations, permits (office, submitted, approved, expiry) with a warning keyed to both expiry and install date, a change request on the job, install and crane scheduling, and a full-screen shop view; it is built structure, not governed by the native-board rule. The item grain is open, with a leaning: the job as the parent row; signs or sign packages as child rows that each move through the six stations, the job showing a roll-up; permits as their own rows linked to the job or the building, each with its expiry and the install date it guards; a small job (one set of channel letters) stays a single row. A monday constraint to carry: all subitems of a board share one column set, so signs (stations) and permits (expiry) cannot both be subitems cleanly, and one of them likely needs its own connected board. To settle with the client: how independently signs move through the shop, and how permits map to signs, buildings and install dates. The change request carries its source (who heard it, through which channel), what changed, the sign or signs it affects, the current approved version, and a required shop acknowledgment before the affected signs move on, with a notification to the shop when one is raised; one capture point that the three people who hear of changes can all use (a form is the natural fit), since the estimator's spreadsheet stays where it is and is where the last change got stuck; who may raise one and who approves it is open. CRM carries quotes and accounts on the native boards, detected live once an account exists and recorded per entity before the blueprint maps anything. Service and Dev are not part of this build. Constraints that survive into any shape: the floor reads and does not type. The estimator's spreadsheet is untouched on day one. The accounting system is not written to in v0.1, which rests on the client's relayed expectation of the accountant ('She'd want to know it doesn't touch the accounting system.', cue 236; 'Which it won't, I assume.', cue 237) and on nothing stronger; writeback and integration direction beyond that are unresolved and v0.1 does not depend on either; staying clear of the system is our safe default, labelled as ours. assumptions.statement: Signs of one job spread across stations, so a sign or sign package is the row that moves; a small job is one row.
assumptions.question: Ruairi: when the hospital runs, will one building's signs be in router, paint and wiring at the same time, or does a job move as a block?

assumptions.statement: A sign package (one building's set, or one sign type) is the workable child row for the hospital; two hundred rows per job is too many to move by hand.
assumptions.question: Ruairi: what do you move as a unit on the wall, a sign or a batch?

assumptions.statement: Permits get their own connected board and signs are subitems of the job, because subitems of one board share one column set.
assumptions.question: Nkechi and Ruairi: does a permit belong to a building, a sign set or the whole job?

assumptions.statement: The six stations are the complete, ordered list and every product passes through all of them.
assumptions.question: Ruairi: is router, paint, letters, wiring, crating, install complete and in order, and does vinyl or vehicle work skip stations?

assumptions.statement: The permit warning fires a fixed number of days before expiry, measured against the install date, and goes to Nkechi and Rosamund.
assumptions.question: Nkechi: how far ahead, per office, and who should see it?

assumptions.statement: The permit offices are the city, the county and two suburbs, each with one clock and one expiry period.
assumptions.question: Nkechi: which offices, with what clock and expiry period each?

assumptions.statement: Ruairi owns the install date in the first version and Lyle tells him when it moves.
assumptions.question: Ruairi and Lyle: who owns the install date, and who hears first when the landlord moves it?

assumptions.statement: A change request may be raised by Ottilie, Rosamund or Lyle through one form, and Rosamund approves it.
assumptions.question: Rosamund: who may raise a change request and who approves it?

assumptions.statement: The three people who hear of changes will use the form; the estimator raising one from her desk is the weak link.
assumptions.question: Ottilie: when a landlord calls you with a change, will you file it before you re-quote?

assumptions.statement: Crane bookings are a date and a confirmed flag on the install; the rental outfit is not in monday.
assumptions.question: Ruairi or Lyle: who books the crane, and how does the outfit confirm?

assumptions.statement: Quotes reach the Quotes board by a one-way import of customer, amount, date sent and last contact; Ottilie keys nothing twice.
assumptions.question: Ottilie: is a one-way import of those fields acceptable, and which fields does it leave out?

assumptions.statement: Landlords, general contractors, tenants and the hospital system are tracked as accounts with a type column; named contacts are not tracked in the first version.
assumptions.question: Rosamund: are the named people at landlords and general contractors to be tracked?

assumptions.statement: The first version seeds permits from Nkechi's spreadsheet (job numbers and dates, amounts removed) and invents sample data for everything else.
assumptions.question: Nkechi: what may the spreadsheet seed, and what must stay out?

assumptions.statement: Rosamund reads the board from the office; the shop reads a full-screen view; nobody on the floor types.
assumptions.question: Ruairi: what must be readable from the floor, and is a read-only full-screen view enough?

assumptions.statement: The owner attends the eighth at seven-thirty.
assumptions.question: Rosamund: has he said yes?

assumptions.statement: The user's own account is the build target; the client's eventual account, tier and seats are a handover question (A21).
assumptions.question: At handover: which account, who administers it, which products and seats?

questions.text: The hospital job: two hundred and some signs, four buildings, forty-one permits. When it runs, will one building's signs be in router, paint and wiring at the same time, and does each permit belong to a building, a sign set or the whole job? The first version leans to the job as the parent row, signs or sign packages as rows under it through the six stations, and permits as their own rows linked to the job or building with the install date each guards; small jobs stay one row.
